h1: The 7 Best Shark Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Shark Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best Shark robot vacuums of 2026, covering AI Ultra, Matrix Plus mop combos and Navigator budget models.
summary: The Shark AI Ultra AV2511AE is the best Shark robot vacuum, with AI home mapping, Matrix Clean navigation and Self-Empty compatibility. The AV2501S adds a HEPA bagless base aimed at pet hair, and the Matrix Plus AV2610WA vacuums and mops. The RV2120AE includes a Self-Empty base, the AV2613WA and UR2650WS are cheaper mop combos, and the AV2120 is the plain entry model.
intro: Shark's robot lineup is hard to read because the names carry so little information. An AI Ultra, a Matrix Plus and a Navigator can look alike on a shelf while one empties itself, one mops and one does neither. Choosing by color and price is how people end up with a dockless robot that needs a bin emptied every day, or a mop pad on a floor of thick rug.

Our editors read the spec sheets for seven Shark models and ranked them on the Primea score, with navigation family, dock, mopping, floor suitability and price bucket doing most of the work. Listings differ in what ships in the box, so we read the title and bullets closely. Suction and runtime figures are not published for these models, so we do not compare them.

products.name: Shark AI Ultra Robot Vacuum, AV2511AE
products.verdict: The smartest Shark for navigation and home mapping.
products.description:
The AV2511AE combines AI home mapping with Matrix Clean navigation and is Self-Empty compatible. It is vacuum only and sits in the $200 to $500 bracket. Mapping lets the robot remember rooms and plan straight passes, instead of bumping around and covering floor twice, which is where the cheaper navigation families lose time.

It ranks first because navigation is what separates a good robot from a frustrating one, and this is the most capable Shark here. The AV2501S brings a dock, but with simpler mapping.

Buy it for a larger home or anyone who wants the best Shark navigation. The caveats are that it does no mopping and the dock bundle needs checking, since compatible does not mean included. Skip it if you want mopping built into the robot.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the best Shark navigation and mapping.
products.skipIf: You want mopping built into the robot.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Matrix Clean
products.verdict: A HEPA bagless base built around pet hair.
products.description:
The AV2501S uses Matrix Clean mapping with a bagless HEPA self-empty base with 30 days of capacity, and it targets pet hair. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket. A base that holds a month of debris means you handle the dust far less often, and HEPA filtration traps fine pet dander.

It ranks second because it brings the dock the AV2511AE lacks in the box, though with less advanced mapping. Bagless also means no bag purchases, only a bin to empty. It edges the RV2120AE on filtration and mapping.

Buy it if you own shedding pets and want a dock without bag costs. The caveats are that it does no mopping and its mapping is simpler than the AI Ultra's. Skip it if you need wet cleaning on hard floors.
products.idealFor: Pet owners wanting a dock and no bag costs.
products.skipIf: You need wet cleaning on hard floors.

products.name: SharkMatrix Plus 2-in-1 Robot Vacuum & Mop, AV2610WA
products.verdict: One robot for vacuuming and mopping mixed floors.
products.description:
The AV2610WA is a 2-in-1 vacuum and mop with Matrix navigation, a Black and Brass finish and Self-Empty compatibility, priced in the $200 to $500 bracket. Combining both jobs means one robot handles dust and a light wet wipe in the same run.

It ranks third because mopping adds value that the vacuum-only AI Ultra models skip, though it leaves out the AI home mapping and does not guarantee a dock in the box. Against the AV2613WA, it carries a more detailed listing.

Buy it for homes mixing hard floors and carpet. The caveats are no AI mapping and a dock that may be separate. Skip it if you only need vacuuming and want the smartest navigation, because the AI Ultra serves that better.
products.idealFor: Homes mixing hard floors and carpet.
products.skipIf: You only need vacuuming and want AI mapping.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, RV2120AE
products.description:
The RV2120AE includes a Self-Empty base, SmartPath navigation and a bagless dock, and it is vacuum only in the $200 to $500 bracket. SmartPath is Shark's simpler navigation, covering floors in orderly rows without building a saved map.

It ranks fourth because it delivers the dock convenience of the AI Ultra line with simpler navigation. It beats the dockless AV2120 by removing the daily bin chore, and it costs less than the AI Ultra models.

Buy it if you want a dock without flagship pricing. The caveats are simpler navigation and no mopping, so skip it if you want advanced mapping or wet cleaning. It is the sensible buy for a small home with a busy schedule.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a dock without flagship pricing.
products.skipIf: You want advanced mapping or mopping.

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1 Robot Vacuum & Mop, AV2613WA
products.verdict: A lower-cost way into the Matrix Plus mop system.
products.description:
The AV2613WA is another 2-in-1 vacuum and mop with Matrix navigation and a Black and Brass finish, positioned at mid-range pricing in the $200 to $500 bracket. It sits close to the AV2610WA in function, which makes the ranking gap about listing detail, not capability.

It ranks fifth because the spec sheet lists fewer details than the AV2610WA, such as no dock note. It exists for buyers who want the mopping system at a lower cost. Against the UR2650WS, it uses the same Matrix line with a better-documented navigation.

Buy it if you want mopping at a modest price. The caveats are the thinner listing and an unconfirmed dock. Skip it if you need a confirmed self-empty setup, because the RV2120AE states it plainly.
products.idealFor: Shoppers wanting mopping at a lower cost.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed self-empty dock.

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus Robot Vacuum and Mop, UR2650WS
products.verdict: A compact budget mop combo for hard floor homes.
products.description:
The UR2650WS is a vacuum and mop combo with a compact profile in the budget 2-in-1 tier, focused on hard floors, in the $200 to $500 bracket. A compact body fits under low furniture and works well in apartments with little clutter.

It ranks sixth because the hard floor focus narrows its appeal compared with the AV-series Matrix Plus models. Its compact body is its advantage in tight spaces, but it is less suited to carpet, and its feature list is shorter.

Buy it for apartments with mostly hard floors. The caveats are weaker carpet suitability and fewer listed features. Skip it if you have a lot of carpet or rugs, since a mop pad and thick pile do not mix.
products.skipIf: You have a lot of carpet.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum, SmartPath Navigation, AV2120
products.verdict: The no-frills Shark for people who just want clean floors.
products.description:
The AV2120 is a compact, white, vacuum-only robot with SmartPath navigation in the $100 to $200 bracket. It has no mop and no dock. That simplicity is the point: a small robot that runs on a schedule and asks nothing else of you.

It ranks last because it lacks the dock of the RV2120AE and the mapping of the AI Ultra line. It is simply the cheapest way into the brand, and the bin needs emptying more often.

Buy it for small spaces and first-time robot owners. The caveat is that there is no self-empty dock or mopping, so skip it if you want either, or if you have a large home where a small bin fills quickly.
products.idealFor: Small spaces and first-time robot owners.
products.skipIf: You want a dock or mop.

whatMatters.detail: Shark uses AI home mapping, Matrix navigation and SmartPath across the range. Mapping systems plan routes and remember rooms, while simpler ones cover floors less efficiently. Check the listing for the exact navigation name before buying, and expect the best coverage from the AI mapping on the AV2511AE. Simpler systems tend to retrace ground.

Self-Empty compatible means the robot works with a base but may not ship with one. A model with the base included will be clearly stated, as with the RV2120AE. Read the title and bullets, because the price gap between the two can be large, and a compatible-only listing means a second purchase.

Bagless bases like the one on the AV2501S avoid bag purchases but need the bin emptied and rinsed. Bag systems stay cleaner but cost more over time. Choose based on whether you prefer chores or consumables, and note that HEPA filtration is the part that keeps allergens inside the base. Empty the bin outdoors if you have allergies.

2-in-1 models wipe hard floors with a damp pad, saving a separate chore. They add a water tank and are not suited to thick carpet. Only pay for it if hard floors dominate your home, and check the listing for carpet handling, since a pad dragging over a rug is a common complaint. Lift pads on rugs by keeping the robot off them.

Shark releases many near-identical model numbers, such as AV2610WA and AV2613WA. Small suffix differences can mean different bundles. Compare the bullet lists, not just the product name, and note the dock, mopping and color details before you click, since two listings can look the same. A few dollars can hide a missing base.

faq.q: Does every Shark robot include a self-empty base?
faq.a: No. Some include it, like the RV2120AE, while others are only Self-Empty compatible. Read the product title and bullets before ordering to see which applies. The price difference between the two types is often larger than the base itself.

faq.q: What is the biggest Shark buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming a model number tells you the features. Near-identical numbers, such as the AV2610WA and AV2613WA, can differ in dock or mopping. Compare the bullet lists carefully, since a missing base changes the real cost.

faq.q: Is the AI Ultra worth it over a Navigator?
faq.a: If you want better mapping and a smarter route, yes. For a small, simple space, a Navigator like the RV2120AE is enough. The dock is the other deciding factor.

faq.q: How do I set up a Shark robot?
faq.a: Place the base on a hard floor by a wall, charge the robot and use the app to map your home. Run a first clean with doors open, then set schedules. Let it finish a full map before adding no-go zones.

Clear hair from the brush roll, wash or replace filters and empty or rinse the bin as needed. Wipe the sensors regularly, because a dusty sensor makes the robot wander. Mop pads on the AV2610WA and other 2-in-1 models need washing.

It vacuums carpet but should not mop it. Look for carpet handling noted on the listing, and keep the mop off rugs on the AV2610WA, AV2613WA and UR2650WS. Closing the door to carpeted rooms is the simplest fix.

finalTake: Buy the AV2511AE for the smartest navigation, and the AV2501S if pet hair is the main problem. The AV2610WA suits homes mixing hard floors and carpet, while the RV2120AE is the budget way to get a dock. The AV2613WA, UR2650WS and AV2120 serve narrower needs. Read the title for the dock and mopping details, because near-identical model numbers hide big differences.
